method: Structured evaluator walkthrough of the phase-3 prototype using synthetic, non-protected fixture content.
privacy: No participant identity, tenant secrets, project plaintext, credentials, or protected artifact content was collected. Fixtures use public work-item IDs and redacted summaries only.

questions.success: Names a derived reason and follows its source without treating attention as priority or mutation.
Names the blocker, authority/time cue, and next inspection action; does not confuse blocked with rejected or stale.
Separates run identity/lifecycle from work-item lifecycle and identifies actor/time/latest evidence.
Identifies the missing category and distinguishes missing, blocked, unavailable, and locked artifact states.
Traces event type, actor, time, and object reference while treating narrative as redacted/non-authoritative when needed.
Identifies pending/accepted/rejected/rework and understands that independent review, not this read-only surface, decides acceptance.

measures.unit: seconds to first correct answer; errors are wrong state/authority or destination; ignoredElements are salient labels not referenced; stateConfusion is a mistaken state pair; signalUsefulness is useful/decorative/unclear.

responsiveNotes.mobile: All six questions were answerable without horizontal scroll; evidence metadata was slowest and required one extra scroll.
responsiveNotes.tablet: All surfaces remained scannable; state gallery competed with evidence content below the fold.
responsiveNotes.desktop: Workspace hierarchy was fastest; detail sidebar authority cues were less prominent.

findings.question: Q2
findings.evidence: One incorrect answer mapped the red blocked rail to review rejection before reading the cause.
findings.decision: Revise: make blocker reason and changed time the first text after the blocked label; retain the barrier cue.

findings.question: Q3
findings.evidence: One answer treated the active run summary as proof that the work item was accepted.
findings.decision: Revise: add a plain-language boundary beside run metadata: Run status is not work-item acceptance.

findings.question: Q4
findings.evidence: Two errors confused absent validation evidence with an unavailable source; exact target and redaction copy were often ignored.
findings.decision: Revise: place a compact missing/source/protected-artifact row before the evidence list.

findings.question: Q6
findings.evidence: Reviewer role was skipped on desktop because the sidebar decision panel competed with the main detail heading.
findings.decision: Accepted risk: Angular must preserve reviewer role beside verdict and timestamp in the first review block.

findings.question: Q1
findings.evidence: Inspection need was read as a priority score once despite the derived-signal explanation.
findings.decision: Revise: replace ordering copy with inspection context and repeat not a priority score beside the count.

findings.question: Q5
findings.evidence: Event ID was ignored, but actor, time, and object reference remained understood.
findings.decision: Accepted risk: event ID remains available for provenance/support without competing with human translation.

revisions.change: Added explicit blocker explanation and changed-time cue in the detail meaning panel.
Added run-versus-acceptance boundary copy beside current execution.
Added evidence status summary naming missing category, source status, and protected artifact boundary.
Clarified attention ordering as inspection context, not priority.
